evidence.summary: dagger/container-use is an Apache-2.0, Go-based, local-only MCP server + CLI (`container-use stdio`) that gives each coding agent (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, and other MCP-compatible agents) a fresh Dagger-managed container tied to its own git branch, so parallel agents can work without filesystem/process conflicts and a human can inspect, `checkout`, or drop a `terminal` into any agent's environment. It requires no separate account or API key — it attaches to the agent's existing MCP session — but does require a local container runtime. It has CI (build/lint/test/release workflows) and 24 colocated Go test files despite no top-level tests/ directory, but its last tagged release (v0.4.2) is from 2025-08-19, over 13 months stale relative to this 2026-09-22 evidence pull, even though the repo was pushed to 1 day prior. Disposition: keep_but_compare — it overlaps this project's already-selected worktrunk (worktrees) and sandbox-runtime (local isolation) layers; the container-level isolation is a plausible improvement on worktrunk's plain worktrees given this project's own documented gap that worktrees don't isolate shared services, but no executed local comparison (container-use vs. worktrunk+sandbox-runtime on a concurrent multi-worker change) exists yet, so per this project's rule (judge agreement never promotes; only an executed comparison overturns) it cannot move past keep_but_compare today.

evidence.worker_features: Per-agent isolated container + dedicated git branch (parallel workers don't conflict); `list` shows all environments and status; `watch` monitors agent activity in real time; `log [--patch]` shows commit history/commands executed (audit trail); `checkout` lets a human pull an agent's branch into their own IDE; `terminal` opens an interactive shell inside a given agent's container for direct intervention; `diff`/`merge`/`apply` move an agent's changes back into the main tree; `config` manages base images, setup commands, secrets, and per-agent MCP configuration (`config agent`, supporting claude, goose, cursor, etc.).

findings.claim: fit_with_native_workflow: "Fits as an optional MCP server any project's Claude Code or Codex session can attach to locally ... matching C1" and "gives each parallel agent a real Docker/Dagger-backed container"
findings.problem: Attaching the MCP server yields no isolation by itself. A native worker here writes with Edit/Write and runs commands with Bash in its host worktree; those effects bypass the container entirely. Isolation only holds if every file and command effect is routed through container-use's MCP tools, which means replacing the isolated-builder tool allowlist (Read, Edit, Write, Bash, Serena symbol-edit tools) and the native worktree placement the Workflow tool performs. That is a rework of the project's worker contract, not an optional attachment. It also weakens the packet's own C3 'deterministic code can own the effects' reading: effects land on a container-side branch that a host-side `merge`/`apply` step must move back, adding a step the current worktree path does not have.

evidence.fit_with_native_workflow: SWE-ReX would sit alongside, not replace, Claude Code's native worker model. Claude Code Bash/Workflow workers already give deterministic per-task effects inside worktrees (worktrunk-managed) for this repo's fan-out pattern, and anthropics/sandbox-runtime is already the selected local isolation layer. SWE-ReX's differentiator is a purpose-built persistent, interactive shell-session abstraction (recognizing command completion, extracting exit codes, supporting REPL-style tools like ipython/gdb across a session) addressable through a Python SDK or REST server, and pluggable across local/Docker/Modal/AWS/Fargate/Daytona backends without changing agent code — something the incumbents' one-shot Bash-per-call model does not offer natively. It would only be adopted for a scenario needing a long-lived, resumable, cross-backend shell session (e.g., an interactive debugger or REPL workflow spanning many turns), not as a general Bash replacement.
evidence.interface: Python SDK (pip install `swe-rex`, with extras for `[modal]`, `[fargate]`, `[daytona]`) built around Deployment and Runtime classes, plus a REST server (`RemoteRuntime`/`RemoteDeployment`) exposing the same session/exec API over HTTP so a client can drive a remote sandbox. Core capability is persistent, interactive shell sessions: the runtime detects when a submitted command has finished, extracts stdout/stderr and exit code, and lets an agent run further commands or interactive tools (ipython, gdb, etc.) in the same session — supporting many such sessions in parallel across processes/machines.
evidence.isolation_model: Pluggable deployment backends selected by config, not a single sandbox: Local (bare subprocess, no isolation/credentials), Docker or Podman containers, Modal (serverless cloud sandboxes, needs a Modal token), AWS Fargate (needs AWS credentials/IAM), Daytona (WIP as of v1.4.0, needs Daytona account/token), plus a Dummy backend for testing and a Remote backend that talks to any already-running swerex server. Each deployment is a separate, independently addressable sandbox instance; there is no described shared global state between deployments, so effects are ownable per deployment/session in the way the criteria describe for worktrees/sandboxes.

evidence.auth_model: Dual: (1) API key forwarding — coop forwards ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY to the guest via SSH SendEnv, resolved from config.toml or the host env var; keys are "never written to disk inside the guest." (2) Native account login — for Claude Code, if no key is forwarded, the user runs `/login` inside `coop ca` (or `coop claude`) to interactively sign in with their own Claude account, and Claude Code's own daemon persists that session across `coop ca` reattaches ("Background sessions are managed by Claude Code (not by coop)... reopening `coop ca` reattaches to whatever Claude Code's daemon is still running"). For Codex, coop explicitly documents a second mode, `auth = "chatgpt"`, which uses "a ChatGPT account or ChatGPT Business workspace with Codex instead of an OpenAI API key," with credentials cached in the guest's keyring and first login done via `coop codex -- login --device-auth`. No separate coop-specific account is created in either case; the VM either receives a forwarded host key or the user logs into their own Anthropic/OpenAI account fresh inside the guest. (Codex additionally supports codex_login/ChatGPT login; the schema's single enum only records one value.)
evidence.summary: trailofbits/coop is a Rust CLI (Apache-2.0, v0.6.0 released 2026-09-09, pushed 2026-09-17) that provisions disposable Firecracker microVMs (Linux) or Lima VMs (macOS arm64) and runs Claude Code or Codex CLI inside them with full tool access (Docker, git, compilers) isolated from the host. It supports both forwarded API keys and the user's own native Claude/ChatGPT account login inside the guest, with Claude Code's background-session daemon surviving `coop ca` reattaches. It has a tests/ directory and multi-workflow CI (ci.yml, claude-review.yml, codex-review.yml, release.yml), and exposes several commands with `--json` output (status, list, images, up --dry-run) but no documented SDK, streaming structured-event protocol, resumable-session API, or MCP/custom-tool dispatch layer distinct from what Claude Code/Codex already provide inside the guest. Host requirements are Linux x86_64 (arm64 "available but untested") with a writable /dev/kvm and sudo, or macOS Apple Silicon with Lima; WSL2 is not mentioned anywhere in the read docs, so /dev/kvm/nested-virtualization support under WSL2 is unverified.
evidence.interface: CLI only (`coop up`, `coop claude`, `coop codex`, `coop ca`/`claude-agents`, `coop shell/stop/destroy`), with `--json` flags on several inspection/status/dry-run subcommands for machine-readable output; no documented SDK or exec/headless streaming-events mode beyond what Claude Code/Codex themselves provide once inside the guest.
evidence.isolation_model: VM-level isolation: Firecracker microVM on Linux, Lima (Apple Virtualization.framework) on macOS. Filesystem: guest is the isolation perimeter; files pulled from guest to host (workspace.rs) are treated as untrusted, called "the widest guest→host channel." Network: on Firecracker, TAP ports marked isolated, iptables FORWARD rules block guest-to-guest routing, port-forwards bind to 127.0.0.1 only; on Lima, each guest gets its own per-instance network stack. Credentials: by default travel via SSH SendEnv/stdin (never argv); an optional credential proxy (issue #411) keeps real API keys on the host and gives the guest capability tokens instead, but its jailing "degrades by kernel version: full confinement on kernel >=6.7, degraded on 5.13-6.6, refused on older kernels." Inside the guest there is deliberately no privilege boundary: the guest user has passwordless sudo and Claude runs with bypassPermissions. Guest-to-guest isolation is pairwise, not absolute, and coop disables host-key checking so a guest can impersonate peers.
evidence.worker_features: Multiple named VM instances per project directory via `coop up --new-instance --name <name>` ("useful for running two agents against the same source tree"), each independently started/stopped/destroyed by name (`coop shell`, `coop stop`, `coop destroy`), optionally sharing state via `--mount`. `coop ca` (claude-agents) opens Claude Code's own agent view inside the guest; background sessions are owned and persisted by Claude Code's daemon, not by coop, so closing/reopening `coop ca` reattaches rather than restarting. No coop-level programmatic dispatch, worker-pool abstraction, or task-queue API was found in the docs read; orchestration across instances is manual CLI invocation.
evidence.structured_events: No streaming/structured-event protocol (e.g., stream-json) or SDK-level event stream was found for coop itself.
